backlog.spec: Pass jac= to minimize with the analytic Jacobian of cons(v) and the constant objective gradient (-1 on radius entries). Build it with vectorized numpy over the iu pairs: for pair (i,j) fill the distance derivatives with respect to centres i and j and -1 for radii i and j; boundary rows are simple sparse entries. This removes finite-difference cost so SLSQP can run many more iterations within the time budget.
backlog.title: Analytic constraint Jacobian for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Move the centre limits into SLSQP's bounds argument (centres in [0,1], radii in [0,0.5]) and keep only the pairwise non-overlap inequalities plus containment inequalities c-r>=0 and 1-c-r>=0 in cons. This shrinks the constraint vector and removes the post-optimisation clip of centres.
backlog.title: Variable bounds instead of box constraints

backlog.spec: Include in cons only pairs whose centres are closer than a cutoff (for example 2*max radius + 0.15) at the start of each SLSQP call. After solving, recompute all pair distances; if any excluded pair overlaps, add those pairs and re-solve, for at most 3 rounds. This speeds each iteration while keeping the final packing valid.
backlog.title: Sparse neighbour-pair constraints with lazy re-check

backlog.spec: After an initial random SLSQP solve, repeatedly perturb the current best packing: add Gaussian noise of scale 0.03 to all centres and multiply radii by a random factor in [0.8,1.0], re-run SLSQP from there and repair. Keep the new packing only if its repaired radius sum is higher. Occasionally (about one time in five) start from a fresh random initialisation so the search does not stall.
backlog.title: Basin hopping around the incumbent

backlog.spec: From the current best packing, delete the smallest circle and reinsert it at the candidate point (among 2000 random samples) with the largest clearance to all other circles and the walls. Re-run SLSQP from this configuration and keep the result only if the repaired radius sum improves.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert smallest circle

backlog.spec: Identify rattlers, meaning circles with fewer than two near-contacts (gap below 1e-4) in the current best packing. Move each rattler to a random location and re-optimise with SLSQP; keep the result if it improves the repaired sum. This targets wasted space without disturbing the jammed core.
backlog.title: Rattler relocation move

backlog.spec: Generate the eight images of the best packing under the symmetry group of the square (rotations by 90 degrees and reflections) and use each as a warm start for SLSQP. Keep whichever gives the highest repaired sum. This is cheap extra exploration of already-good configurations.
backlog.title: Global symmetry images of the best packing

backlog.spec: In the basin hopping loop, accept a perturbed-and-reoptimised packing with a worse radius sum when exp((new - old)/T) exceeds a uniform draw, where T decays geometrically from 0.01 to 1e-4 over the time budget. Always track the best packing seen separately from the current one.
backlog.title: Simulated-annealing acceptance in basin hopping

backlog.spec: In the perturbation step of basin hopping, set the centre noise standard deviation to decay geometrically from 0.08 at the start to 0.005 near the end of the time budget, measured by elapsed process time. Early large jumps explore; late small jumps refine.
backlog.title: Decaying perturbation scale

backlog.spec: Run many cheap random starts with a small MAX_ITER (for example 40). Keep the top 10 percent by repaired radius sum and continue only those with a larger iteration budget, then keep the best of the survivors. Repeat the halving until the time budget is used. This spends more time on promising starts.
backlog.title: Successive halving over random starts

backlog.spec: Maintain a pool of the 8 best packings. Create offspring by taking the centres from one parent for circles with x below a random cut value and from the other parent for the rest, then match circle counts and run SLSQP from that child. Replace the worst pool member if the child is better. Use fresh random starts when the pool is not yet full.
backlog.title: Elite population with crossover

backlog.spec: Start each restart with a random set of centres and all radii set to zero, then first maximise the radius sum with only the containment constraints and a small penalty for overlap, then run the full SLSQP with all constraints. This gives the optimiser a feasible-looking start and reduces early infeasible wandering.
backlog.title: Radii-first two-stage initialisation

backlog.spec: Before the exact SLSQP solve, run L-BFGS-B on a smooth penalty objective: minus the radius sum plus a weight times the squared overlap and containment violations. Increase the weight over five stages (for example 10 to 1e5). Use the output as the SLSQP start. This is cheap compared with SLSQP and gives a near-feasible start.
backlog.title: Penalty continuation before SLSQP

backlog.spec: Start from random centres with tiny radii and repeatedly grow each radius toward the largest value that does not overlap its neighbours, moving centres slightly apart when two circles touch. Stop when no radius can grow more than a small threshold, then polish with SLSQP. This produces dense jammed starts.
backlog.title: Inflation (Lubachevsky-style) start

backlog.spec: Build starts from hexagonal or square lattice patches with 32 points chosen as the centres of a lattice cropped to the square, with random rows removed or added to reach 32 centres. Assign radii as uniform small values. Use these as some of the restarts alongside uniform random starts.
backlog.title: Hexagonal-lattice seeded starts

backlog.spec: Initialise radii not as a constant 0.05 but from a random draw such as a uniform in [0.02, 0.12], and place centres uniformly at random. Diversifying initial size distributions gives SLSQP different contact graphs to converge to.
backlog.title: Random heterogeneous radius initialisation

backlog.spec: Replace the iterative pairwise shrink loop in repair with a global computation: compute for each pair the ratio of distance to radius sum and for each circle the containment slack, then scale the radii by the minimum of these ratios (or shrink each radius to its own limit with a single pass). Verify with a strict check and fall back to the existing repair if the check fails.
backlog.title: Exact feasibility scaling in repair

backlog.spec: After the best packing is found, refine it with sequential linear programming: linearise the near-active constraints at the current point, solve a linear program with scipy linprog that maximises the radius sum within a trust region of radius 1e-3, accept the step if the true constraints remain satisfied, and shrink the trust region otherwise. Repeat until the gain is negligible.
backlog.title: Final active-set LP polish

backlog.spec: Use scipy minimize with method trust-constr on the best packing, with sparse Jacobian and Hessian-free updates, as a final refinement step with a small share of the time budget. Keep whichever of the SLSQP and trust-constr results has the larger valid radius sum.
backlog.title: Trust-constr final polish

backlog.spec: Rescale the optimisation variables so centres and radii are of comparable magnitude, for example optimise over 10 times the radii and centres or normalise the objective by its value at the start. This improves SLSQP conditioning and step quality. Unscale before repair.
backlog.title: Variable scaling for conditioning

backlog.spec: Raise MAX_ITER from 200 to 1000 and set SLSQP ftol to 1e-12 so that restarts run to convergence rather than stopping early at 200 iterations. Check the iteration count returned by the solver and keep the time check in the outer loop.
backlog.title: Looser SLSQP tolerance and iteration budget

backlog.spec: Raise TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.93, so each call uses about 28 s of the 30 s CPU budget and stays well under the 45 s void threshold. Keep the time check based on time.process_time as it is now.
backlog.title: Use more of the CPU budget

backlog.spec: Add a small safety margin in repair so the returned radii are strictly feasible under double precision: subtract a margin of 1e-12 from each radius after scaling and keep the SHRINK constant as a floor. This avoids borderline overlaps caused by rounding in SLSQP output.
backlog.title: Minimum-radius exclusion tolerance

backlog.spec: Add a small quadratic penalty on deviation of each radius from the mean radius inside the objective (weight 1e-3). This pushes starts toward more uniform sizes first and lets SLSQP escape early local optima before the true objective is restored in a final unpenalised solve.
backlog.title: Noisy restarts with weight decay on radii

backlog.spec: For the first half of the SLSQP iterations, include only the pairs whose centres are closest at the start, and then include all pairs for the second half. Acts as a regulariser on the constraint set that reduces early oscillation.
backlog.title: Dropout of constraints during early iterations

backlog.spec: Each SLSQP call uses a random subset of about 60 percent of the non-overlap pairs, chosen with the seed-driven RNG, and a full check is run at the end with repair. Different subsets across calls diversify the search path.
backlog.title: Mini-batch of constraints per SLSQP call

backlog.spec: Within one solve call, split the time budget into several independent random sub-searches and compare their best repaired radius sums, keeping the best. Equivalent to restarts but with each sub-search using a different constraint ordering and initial scale.
backlog.title: Multiple random seeds per call of solve

backlog.spec: Generate starts that are symmetric about the vertical or horizontal midline: place random centres in one half and mirror them, with an even or odd split so that exactly 32 circles result. Symmetric starts are often near good packings and reduce the effective search dimension.
backlog.title: Symmetric (mirror-symmetric) initial configurations

backlog.spec: In solve, first optimise a packing of n+1 circles with the existing _solve_once and _repair (same time-budget logic). Remove the circle with the smallest radius, giving n circles. Then run the existing basin-hopping loop from that n-circle packing, with the same random-number stream seeded by seed. Keep the rest of train.py unchanged. Return the best valid packing for n circles. The extra circle gives the search room to rearrange before one is removed.
backlog.title: Over-pack n+1 circles, then drop the smallest

backlog.spec: Replace the single SLSQP call in _solve_once with an augmented Lagrangian scheme. Keep a multiplier vector lambda for every pair, wall and radius constraint, initialised at zero. Each outer iteration minimises -sum(r) + sum(lambda*g) + (rho/2)*sum(max(0,g)^2) with SLSQP, where g >= 0 are the constraint values. Then update lambda = max(0, lambda - rho*g) and increase rho by a factor of 2 if violation has not dropped. Stop after about 5 outer iterations or when the maximum violation is below 1e-9. Pass the result to the existing _repair. The goal is a smoother path to a feasible local optimum than a single hard-constraint solve.
backlog.title: Augmented Lagrangian outer loop around SLSQP

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, replace the objective -sum(r) with -sum(w_i * r_i), where w_i is drawn from uniform(0.8, 1.2) once per restart using rng. Keep all constraints unchanged. Each restart then climbs to a different local optimum because the weighting tilts which circles grow. Keep the rest of the basin-hopping loop. Every returned packing is still scored by the unweighted sum of radii, so the best packing is chosen by the true objective. This is a cheap way to diversify the local searches.
backlog.title: Random per-circle objective weights

backlog.spec: Add a move to the basin-hopping step. With probability 0.3, pick two circles i and j whose radii differ by more than 20 percent. Swap their centres, keeping each radius where it is, so the big circle sits where the small one was and the reverse. Then run _solve_once from that warm start, repair, and apply the usual accept rule. Otherwise use the existing perturbation. This changes which circles occupy the good spots without losing the packing's overall shape.
backlog.title: Swap-positions move between unequal circles

backlog.spec: In solve, replace the Gaussian perturbation rng.normal(0, 0.05, (n, 2)) with a heavy-tailed draw: rng.standard_cauchy((n, 2)) multiplied by a scale of 0.01 and clipped to [-0.2, 0.2]. Most steps then make small local moves while occasionally a circle jumps far. Keep the acceptance rule and time split unchanged. The idea is to reach distant basins without losing the local refinement that the Gaussian steps give.
backlog.title: Heavy-tailed Cauchy perturbation in basin hopping

backlog.spec: Keep a list of the radius-sum values, rounded to 4 decimals, of every packing accepted in the basin-hopping chain. When a new candidate's rounded sum is already in the list, discard it and do not update cur or best, unless it beats best. This stops the chain from cycling between a few near-identical local optima and pushes it toward new basins. The list is a Python set and adds only a few lines.
backlog.title: Tabu memory of visited packings

backlog.spec: At each basin-hopping step, generate K=4 independent perturbed starts from the current packing with rng, run _solve_once and _repair on each, and keep the one with the largest radius sum as the candidate. Apply the usual acceptance rule to that single candidate. This costs K times more SLSQP calls per step but gives each step a better chance of finding an improving basin. Keep the time split unchanged and stop the loop when the time budget is used.
backlog.title: Best-of-K proposals per basin-hopping step

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping step, perturb only one or two randomly chosen circles per step, instead of all n. Move each chosen circle to a uniform random position in [0,1]^2 with probability 0.5, or jitter its centre by a normal with scale 0.05 otherwise. Set its radius to 0.5 times the minimum radius of the packing before calling _solve_once. Keep the other circles at their current positions in the warm start. This is a more local move that leaves most of the packing intact and suits the many small rearrangements that a dense packing needs.
backlog.title: Local single-circle perturbation moves

backlog.spec: Track the number of basin-hopping steps since the best radius sum last improved. If this count exceeds 30, reset cur to best and reset the temperature schedule so that T restarts at 0.003 and decays to 1e-4 over the remaining budget. Clear the counter. Otherwise keep the existing annealed acceptance and perturbation. The reheat gives the search a fresh chance to leave a plateau without throwing away the best packing found so far.
backlog.title: Stagnation-triggered reheat to best

backlog.spec: Before the hard-constraint SLSQP call, run a smoothed objective. Use the log-sum-exp soft-minimum of the pair gaps (d_ij - r_i - r_j) and wall gaps as a smooth penalty, and maximise sum(r) minus mu times the soft violation with L-BFGS-B over centres and radii. Increase mu from 10 to 1e4 over 6 steps, as a continuation. Then pass the result to the existing SLSQP call with the hard constraints. The soft stage gives a well-conditioned path into the feasible region and is a different smoothing from the hard penalty already on the list.
backlog.title: Soft-min radius objective with sharpness continuation

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, replace the global Gaussian kick with a regional one on about half of the steps. Pick a random centre point in [0,1]^2 and a radius R drawn uniformly from [0.2, 0.4]. Every circle whose centre lies within R of that point gets a fresh uniform random centre inside the square and radius INIT_RADIUS. The others keep their current positions and radii. Run the usual SLSQP solve and _repair on the result, and keep the usual acceptance rule. Keep the other half of the steps as the current small global perturbation. Nothing else changes.
backlog.title: Large-neighbourhood destroy-and-repair

backlog.spec: Add a second hop type to basin hopping that moves the whole packing rather than individual circles. With probability 0.3, scale all centres about (0.5, 0.5) by a factor s drawn uniformly from [0.9, 1.1], then clip to [0,1] and shrink radii to fit before the SLSQP solve. Otherwise use the existing Gaussian perturbation. Use the same acceptance rule. This targets whole-basin shifts, which per-circle noise rarely produces.
backlog.title: Global compression and expansion move

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed perturbation sd of 0.05 with a small set of scales {0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.2}. Keep a running score for each scale: the exponentially averaged improvement of the sum of radii over the current best when that scale was used. Choose the scale each step with softmax over the scores, with a minimum selection probability of 0.05 so that every scale stays alive. Update the score after each solve. All randomness still comes from the seed. Leave the acceptance temperature schedule unchanged.
backlog.title: Adaptive operator selection over perturbation scales

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP solve in the hop loop, run a short interior-point stage. Maximise sum(r) + mu * sum(log(slack)) over all pair and wall slacks, using L-BFGS-B on the centres and radii with slacks clamped to a small positive floor. Take mu from 1e-2 down to 1e-5 in four geometric steps, with about 50 iterations each. Feed the result into the existing SLSQP call as the starting point. Use a log barrier rather than the soft-min penalty already tried, so the iterate stays strictly feasible throughout.
backlog.title: Log-barrier continuation before the hard SLSQP solve

backlog.spec: Keep the displacement vector (new centres minus old centres) from the last accepted hop. On the next hop, with probability 0.5, start from the current packing plus 1.5 times that stored displacement, clipped to [0,1], and then apply the usual small Gaussian noise (sd 0.01) before SLSQP. Otherwise use the usual Gaussian hop. Store the displacement again whenever a hop is accepted. This reuses directions that recently improved the packing.
backlog.title: Momentum extrapolation of accepted hops

backlog.spec: Track the number of consecutive basin-hopping steps without a new best. When that count reaches 25, discard the current chain and start a fresh random SLSQP packing from _solve_once with new random draws, keeping the global best across restarts. Reset the stagnation counter and the temperature clock for the new chain, so the temperature decays over one chain's time. Chains therefore restart when they plateau, rather than cooling at a fixed rate.
backlog.title: Stagnation-triggered fresh restart

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random initial centres in _solve_once with a Halton sequence in bases 2 and 3, mapped into [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]. Apply a random offset and a random permutation of the points taken from the seed-driven rng, so that different seeds give different starts. Keep the radii initialised at INIT_RADIUS. Use this only for fresh starts; hops keep the current Gaussian perturbation. The point is more even coverage of the square at the start.
backlog.title: Low-discrepancy Halton starts

backlog.spec: Add an alternating step after each SLSQP solve. Fix the centres and solve the exact linear programme that maximises sum(r) subject to the pair constraints d_ij >= r_i + r_j and the wall constraints r_i <= distance to each wall, using scipy.optimize.linprog with the HiGHS method. Then run SLSQP on the centres with the new radii as the start. Repeat the pair of steps twice per hop. The LP gives exact radii for fixed centres, which SLSQP handles less well. Make sure the final output still passes _repair.
backlog.title: Alternating block-coordinate optimisation

backlog.spec: After _repair, run a growth pass. Visit the circles in a random order drawn from rng. For each circle, compute the largest radius it can take, which is the minimum of its wall distances and of (distance to each other centre minus that centre's current radius). Set its radius to that value if larger than the current one. Then repeat the pass once more. Only increase radii, so the output stays feasible. Run this on every candidate packing before the acceptance test. It is cheap and can recover slack that the SLSQP solve leaves.
backlog.title: Greedy sequential radius growth

backlog.spec: Run K=4 basin-hopping chains in the same call, each at a fixed temperature from a geometric ladder between 1e-4 and 1e-2. Advance the chains round-robin, one hop each, within the same CPU budget. After every 10 rounds, propose swapping the states of adjacent temperature rungs with the usual Metropolis probability on the difference in sum of radii. Track the global best across all chains. The point is that hot chains explore and cold chains exploit, rather than one annealed chain doing both.
backlog.title: Parallel tempering over hop chains

backlog.spec: Replace the random uniform centres in _solve_once with a greedy placement. Build a grid of about 2000 candidate points in [0,1]^2 with a fixed-size seed-dependent jitter. Place circles one at a time: put circle k at the candidate maximising the distance to its nearest existing centre or wall, capped at 0.15. Give each circle an initial radius equal to half that clearance times a uniform(0.8, 1.0) factor from rng. Then run the existing SLSQP and repair. The point is to start from a space-filling layout rather than random clumps. Keep the rest of the basin-hopping loop unchanged.
backlog.title: Largest-hole greedy start

backlog.spec: Add a small CMA-ES outer loop over the 2n centre coordinates, in place of the random-restart loop for the first 40% of the budget. Use population size about 16, initial step 0.1, and score each candidate by running _repair on the candidate centres with radii from a cheap closed-form estimate (min of wall clearance and half the nearest-neighbour distance). Implement the standard CMA-ES update with numpy only (mean, covariance, evolution paths). When the CMA-ES step size falls below 1e-3 or time runs out, hand the best centres to _solve_once as x0 and continue the existing basin hopping from there.
backlog.title: CMA-ES over centres with SLSQP polish

backlog.spec: Before solving for n circles, solve for n-1 circles with the existing basin hopping for a short fixed slice, about 25% of the budget. Then insert one new circle at the point of largest clearance (sampled on a grid), with radius 0.01, and run _solve_once from that warm start with all n circles. Continue the normal basin hopping on the n-circle packing for the rest of the budget. The aim is to start from a packing that already has a good global structure, so the hops refine rather than search from scratch.
backlog.title: Incremental growth from n-1

backlog.spec: Change the random start in _solve_once so that the four corners of the square each hold one circle with a larger initial radius (0.12 to 0.15). Place the remaining n-4 centres at uniform random positions in [0.1, 0.9]^2, with initial radii drawn from uniform(0.04, 0.08). The corner circles are then free to move in SLSQP, so the start is only a bias and not a fixed structure. Apply this only to the fresh random starts, not to the hop perturbations.
backlog.title: Corner-anchored graded start

backlog.spec: For each fresh start, first find centres that maximise the minimum pairwise distance inside the unit square using a short penalty-based gradient descent (numpy only, about 300 steps with a decreasing step size). Set all radii to half the resulting minimum distance, capped by wall clearance, to get a valid equal-radius packing. Then release the radii as free variables and run the existing SLSQP and repair from the centres of that packing with these radii as the initial radii. This starts from a near-hexagonal equal-circle arrangement and lets radii grow from there.
backlog.title: Equal-radius max-min-distance start then release

backlog.spec: After the final SLSQP and repair of the best packing, identify the active constraints: pairs whose gap is below 1e-7 and walls whose clearance is below 1e-7. Form the nonlinear system of equalities for these contacts in the unknowns (centres, radii). If the system is square or overdetermined, solve it with a few damped Gauss-Newton steps using least squares from numpy. Accept the new configuration only if it stays feasible after the existing repair and its radius sum is higher. This gives a tighter final packing than SLSQP's tolerance limit, without any new package.
backlog.title: Newton solve of the active contact set

backlog.spec: Replace the single basin-hopping chain with a race. Run K=6 independent chains, each starting from its own fresh random SLSQP packing, for 15% of the budget each, using a short per-step maxiter of 50. Keep the top two chains by radius sum and continue only those for the remaining budget, each with its own basin hopping. Each chain uses its own rng stream spawned from the seed, so runs remain reproducible. The aim is to spend early time exploring more basins and late time refining the best.
backlog.title: Racing of parallel short chains

backlog.spec: In _solve_once add a penalty to the SLSQP objective that discourages uneven radii: subtract lambda times the sample variance of r from the objective, where lambda starts at 0.05 and is multiplied by 0.5 at each restart until it reaches zero. Early starts therefore favour packings with similar circle sizes, which often have more contacts, and the final solves use the true objective of sum of radii. Only the objective changes. The constraints and repair are untouched.
backlog.title: Annealed radius-spread penalty

backlog.spec: Add a new perturbation move to the basin-hopping step, used with probability 0.3. Pick a random centre point and select the circles within a radius of 0.25 of it. Rotate those centres about their centroid by a random angle drawn from uniform(-0.3, 0.3) radians, and leave the other circles unchanged. Then run _solve_once from that warm start and apply the existing acceptance rule. This lets whole local domains swap orientation, which the Gaussian per-circle noise cannot do in one step.
backlog.title: Cluster rotation hop

backlog.spec: Give each basin-hopping step a short SLSQP run with maxiter 40 and a tolerance of 1e-6. Every 10th accepted step, run a full solve with maxiter 200 from the current best. The short runs give many cheap hops, and the full runs polish the best basin. Keep the existing repair and acceptance rule. Record the best packing as before so that the final output is always a repaired valid packing.
backlog.title: Two-tier iteration budget per hop

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random centre draw in _solve_once with a Vogel spiral: for k in 0..n-1 set radius_k = sqrt((k+0.5)/n) scaled into [0.1, 0.9] about the centre, angle_k = k * golden_angle, then map to the square. Apply a random global rotation and a jitter of N(0, 0.02) drawn from rng, clip to [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW], and keep INIT_RADIUS. Use this only for the fresh starts; hop steps are unchanged.
backlog.title: Sunflower (Vogel spiral) start with random rotation

backlog.spec: For fresh starts, place the n centres one per cell of the smallest m x m grid with m*m >= n (m = ceil(sqrt(n))). Take a random subset of n cells via rng.permutation, then add a uniform jitter of plus or minus 0.4 cell width to each centre, clipped to [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]. Radii start at INIT_RADIUS. Hop steps and the SLSQP call are unchanged; the only difference is the start geometry.
backlog.title: Jittered stratified-grid start

backlog.spec: In each basin-hopping step, before the SLSQP solve, run 3 to 5 iterations of a weighted Lloyd relaxation on the centres: rasterise the unit square on a 60 x 60 grid, assign each grid point to its nearest centre, and move each centre to the mean of its cell, with a small random step of N(0, 0.01) added. Clip to the square. Then pass the centres with the current radii to the existing SLSQP solve. This spreads crowded circles and opens holes without a large random jump.
backlog.title: Lloyd-style centre spreading as a hop

backlog.spec: Add a hop type to basin hopping: pick a random direction u on the unit circle and a random strength s in [0.02, 0.1]. Move each centre by s times the sign-stable projection of u, plus a small N(0, 0.01) jitter, then clip to the square. Radii are set to 0.9 times their previous values. Then run the usual SLSQP solve and repair. The hop is a directed shear of the whole packing toward one side, which is not a uniform random shake and not a global scaling.
backlog.title: Gravity-shear hop

backlog.spec: For fresh starts, skip SLSQP initially. Place n equal discs of radius 0.01 at random non-overlapping positions. Run a hard-disk Metropolis sweep: propose a move of each disc by N(0, step) and accept only if it stays inside the square and does not overlap any other disc. After each sweep, grow every radius to 0.98 times the maximum radius allowed by the current neighbours and walls. Continue for a fixed number of sweeps, lowering step as the packing densifies. The final configuration is the SLSQP start. This is a stochastic compression, distinct from the deterministic inflation start.
backlog.title: Hard-disk Monte Carlo compression start

backlog.spec: Keep the hard SLSQP constraints but relax the pair-distance and wall constraints by a slack eps: require d_ij - r_i - r_j + eps >= 0 and x_i - r_i + eps >= 0 and the analogous wall terms. Start eps at 1e-2 for the first basin-hopping step of each fresh start, then shrink it by a factor 0.3 each time an SLSQP call succeeds, down to 0 for the last call of each chain. The final result is always repaired with _repair, so a slightly infeasible intermediate is allowed. The aim is to let SLSQP slide circles past small barriers early, then tighten.
backlog.title: Overlap-slack continuation in SLSQP

backlog.spec: Replace the global Gaussian hop in basin hopping with a per-circle scale. For each circle, estimate local free space as the distance to its nearest neighbour minus its radius, and set sigma_i = 0.02 + 0.1 times clip(free space / 0.1, 0, 1). Perturb each centre by N(0, sigma_i) in each coordinate, so crowded circles that cannot move move little and rattlers move more. Keep the rest of the chain as is, including the annealed acceptance.
backlog.title: Free-space-scaled per-circle hop size

backlog.spec: In each basin-hopping step, choose a random 50 percent of the circles and freeze their centres and radii as constants (drop them from the decision vector and from the constraints that involve only frozen circles). Run SLSQP over the free circles with the usual constraints to the frozen ones. Then run one full unfrozen SLSQP solve from the result with maxiter MAX_ITER // 2 and repair. Alternating partial and full solves reduces the variable count per call and changes which contacts the optimiser can reach in one step.
backlog.title: Random frozen-subset SLSQP

backlog.spec: Replace the hand-written accept/reject loop with scipy.optimize.basinhopping on a penalty energy E(c, r) = -sum(r) + mu * sum(max(0, -g)^2), where g ranges over the same pair, wall and nonnegativity terms used in cons. Use an L-BFGS-B local minimiser with analytic gradient, mu = 1e3 fixed, stepsize 0.05, and the seed rng for all randomness. After the search, run one SLSQP solve from the best point with the hard constraints and repair. The time limit is enforced by passing a callback that raises when process_time exceeds the budget.
backlog.title: Scipy basinhopping on the penalty energy

backlog.spec: Break ties between packings with almost equal total radius. Define the score as sum(r) + 1e-4 times the minimum pairwise gap, where gap_ij = d_ij - r_i - r_j over all pairs, and use this score in place of sum(r) for the acceptance test and the best-so-far update. The 1e-4 weight is small enough to never override a real improvement in sum(r) of order 1e-3, but it prefers packings with more uniform spacing, which tend to have more room to move in later hops.
backlog.title: Lexicographic spread tie-break on plateaus

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, replace the pair constraint sqrt(dx^2+dy^2) - ri - rj >= 0 with the smooth form dx^2+dy^2 - (ri+rj)^2 >= 0, and also require ri+rj >= 0 implicitly through the existing r >= 0 bound. Keep the analytic Jacobian from the accepted Jacobian idea, but its pair rows become 2*dx, 2*dy, -2*(ri+rj) for the centres and radii. Leave the wall constraints, the sparse pair selection and the repair step unchanged. The aim is a smoother constraint surface at contact, which should let SLSQP converge in fewer iterations per hop.
backlog.title: Squared-distance pair constraints

backlog.spec: Drop the radii from the search variables entirely. For a given set of centres, define the radii with the existing repair routine (walls, then iterative pairwise shrinking) and score the packing by its sum of radii. Optimise the 2n centre coordinates by a compass or pattern search: for each step size h in a decreasing sequence starting near 0.02, try moving each circle by plus or minus h along each axis, keep any move that increases the score, and halve h when no move helps. Use the remaining time for random restarts of this search and keep the best packing. This removes the nonsmooth radius coupling from SLSQP and tests whether a derivative-free search over the repaired objective escapes the basins that SLSQP gets stuck in.
backlog.title: Centre-only reduced objective with pattern search

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random centre draw in the fresh start with best-candidate sampling: place the first centre uniformly, then for each further centre draw 30 uniform candidates in [0.05, 0.95]^2 and keep the one whose distance to its nearest existing centre (including the walls, measured as the distance to the boundary) is largest. Set the initial radii to a small common value. Pass the result to the existing SLSQP call. Use the seed for all draws. This gives a well-spread, low-clustering start without any new geometry, and it is cheap enough to run for every fresh start.
backlog.title: Best-candidate (Mitchell) start

backlog.spec: Add a hop that is rigidity-aware. After a SLSQP solve, collect the active pair and wall constraints (those with slack below 1e-6). Build the Jacobian of these active constraints with respect to the centres and radii, compute an orthonormal basis of its null space with numpy.linalg.svd, and draw the perturbation as a random combination of those null-space vectors scaled to a norm of 0.05 times the mean radius. Apply this perturbation to the current packing instead of the isotropic Gaussian, and keep the rest of basin hopping unchanged. Moves in the null space leave the contact graph intact to first order, so the hop explores the flexible directions of a packing rather than breaking contacts at random.
backlog.title: Contact-null-space hop

backlog.spec: Run a small differential-evolution loop as an alternative to basin hopping for part of the budget. Keep a population of 12 centre sets, each scored by the repaired sum of radii. For each member, form a mutant from three other members, v = a + 0.6*(b - c), clip to [0,1], then cross it with the target at rate 0.8 coordinate by coordinate. Score the trial after repair and replace the target if the trial is better. After every 10 generations, run the SLSQP polish from the best member. Use the first 40 percent of the time budget for this search and the remainder for the existing basin hopping starting from the best member. The population adds diversity that the single chain lacks.
backlog.title: Differential evolution over centres

backlog.spec: Add a hop that reflects part of the packing. Choose a random line through a random point in the square with a random direction. Reflect the centres of all circles on one side of the line across it, keeping circles on the other side fixed, then clip to [0,1] and pass through the existing SLSQP and repair. Use this move with probability 0.2 in place of the Gaussian perturbation. The reflection creates a seam between two mirrored domains, which the local optimisation then has to heal. This is a different large move from cluster rotation, because it changes the orientation of a whole region at once.
backlog.title: Half-plane reflection hop

backlog.spec: Keep the annealed basin-hopping temperature but adapt its schedule to the observed acceptance rate rather than fixing it by elapsed time alone. Keep a running acceptance fraction over the last 20 hops. Every 20 hops, multiply the temperature T by 0.8 if the acceptance fraction is above 0.4 and by 1.25 if it is below 0.15, and clamp T to [1e-5, 1e-2]. Keep the time-based decay as a floor so that T still falls toward 1e-4 by the end of the budget. This keeps the chain at a useful exploration level whatever the local scale of the packing is, instead of relying on a fixed decay curve.
backlog.title: Acceptance-rate-adaptive temperature

backlog.spec: Before the hard SLSQP solve of each hop, run it with the walls moved inward by a margin m, so the wall constraints become c - r >= m and 1 - c - r >= m. Start with m = 0.02 and reduce it geometrically to 0 across the first two SLSQP calls of each restart, using the warm-start variables from the previous call. The final call uses m = 0, so the returned packing is valid. The inward margin keeps circles off the boundary early, where SLSQP tends to lock circles to walls in poor configurations. This is a regularisation of the boundary, not a change to the pair constraints.
backlog.title: Wall-margin continuation

backlog.spec: Make each basin-hopping step apply several independent local moves at once. Pick four disjoint random subsets of about n/8 circles each from the current packing, perturb each subset with its own Gaussian of scale 0.03, then run one SLSQP call on the combined configuration. Score the result after repair and accept or reject the whole batch with the existing annealed Metropolis rule. This shares the solver cost across several local moves per step, so the chain samples more configurations per 30 seconds, which matters because the current bottleneck is the number of hops.
backlog.title: Mini-batch of hops per SLSQP call

backlog.spec: Replace the SLSQP-only fresh start with a short hard-disk Monte Carlo compression before the solve. Start with n circles of radius 0.01 at random centres. For 2000 sweeps, propose a random displacement of each circle by at most a step size that adapts to keep the acceptance near 40 percent, reject any move that causes an overlap or leaves the square, and after each sweep grow every radius to the largest value that keeps the packing valid, scaled by 0.5 of the gap. Stop when the sum of radii stops increasing. Pass the resulting centres and radii as the starting point to the existing SLSQP call. The compression yields a jammed packing that is generally better than a random uniform start.
backlog.title: Hard-disk Monte Carlo compression start

incumbent.description: Turns the random-restart loop into basin hopping: each step perturbs the current packing's centres and re-optimises with SLSQP, accepts worse packings with probability exp((new-old)/T) under a geometric T schedule from 0.01 to 1e-4, and tracks the best packing separately.

memo: Helped: only basin hopping (slot 3, -2.9355, gain 0.0102, about 3 sd, 1 run). Slot 9 (sparse neighbour pairs) gave -2.9396 and -2.9355 over 2 runs; slot 29 (grid start) gave -2.9396 and -2.9375 over 2 runs. Both are the best so far, but still near noise. Did not help: new starts (inflation -2.9042, mirror -2.9172, rattler -2.9246), greedy hopping (-2.9349), elite pool (-2.9309), soft-min continuation (-2.9270), more iterations (-2.9351), TIME_FRACTION 0.93 (-2.9355). Gains of 0.0015 to 0.0030 (slots 4, 6, 7, 13, 17, 25, 29) are within noise (sd 0.0034); many slots sit near -2.937 to -2.938, so this may be a plateau. Next: replicate slots 9, 17 and 29. Combine sparse pairs, the analytic Jacobian (-2.9380) and the grid start, since faster solves allow more hops. Tune hop size, temperature and time split. Avoid new move types, pools and reheats.
